 Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,
closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 12pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be summarized
by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City Council and will
also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be recorded for
public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Meeting Compensation Disclosure
Pursuant to Government Code Section 54952.3: Disclosure of compensation for meeting
attendance by City Council Members is $790 monthly regardless of the amount of meetings.

Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous
comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials
During this time, members of the City Council will report on matters pertaining to their service
on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City
pursuant to Assembly Bill 1234. City Council Members will also have an opportunity to
comment on matters not on the agenda.

Consent Calendar Items

Agenda Items 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 are Consent Calendar Items. All items including
Ordinances, Resolutions and Contracts, may be approved by adoption of the Consent
Calendar, individually and collectively by one (1) motion. There will be no separate discussion
of these items unless Members of the City Council, the public, or staff request that specific
items be removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion and action. Members
of the public are permitted to speak on any item listed but their time period is limited to three
(3) minutes in total.

Any motion to introduce or adopt an Ordinance on the Consent Calendar shall be: (1) a
motion to waive the reading of the Ordinance and introduce the Ordinance or (2) a motion to
waive the reading of the Ordinance and adopt the Ordinance, as appropriate.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &

  7
 Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers first. After all speakers in the Chambers have spoken,
the Presiding Officer will call upon those participating via zoom or teleconference.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, virtually, email, phone call, mail and any other method which may become
available. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such times when a State of
Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

SUBJECT:  A  PUBLIC  HEARING  ON  A  RESOLUTION  APPROVING  THE  CITY'S
mTENT  TO  APPROVE  AN  AMENDMENT  TO  THE  CONTRACT  WITH  CALIFORNIA
PUBLIC  EMPLOYEES'  RETIREMENT  SYSTEM  TO  IMPLEMENT  A  COST  SHARING
PROGRAM  BETWEEN  THE  CITY  AND  UNREPRESENTED  EXECUTIVE  MANAGEMENT
CONTRACT  EMPLOYEES

PURPOSE:  To consider  adopting  a resolution  giving  notice  of the City's  intent  to approve  a contract
amendment  between  the City  of South  Gate ("City")  and the Board  of Administration  of the California
Public  Employees'  Retirement  System  ("CalPERS")  to implement  a cost sharing  program  between  the
unrepresented  executive  management  contract  employees  ("Executives").

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The  City  Council  will  conduct  a public  hearing  on  a request  to
consider  adopting  a Resolution  giving  notice  of the City's  intention  to approve  an amendment  to the
contract  between  the  City  and  the  Board  of  Administration  of  the  California  Public  Employees'
Retirement  System  (CalPERS)  to provide  employee  cost sharing  of 1% for the unrepresented  executive
management  contract  employees  effective  on December  17, 2023.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  The estimated  savings  from  implementing  the cost sharing  program  is $17,600  in
Fiscal  Year 2023-2024  and will  progressively  grow  by the annual  wage increases  each year thereafter.

NOTICING  REQUIREMENTS:  A public  hearing  notice  was  duly  published  in the South  Gate
Press,  a newspaper  of general  circulation,  on September  21, 2023.

ANALYSIS:  None

BACKGROUND:  The City's  current  contract  with  CalPERS  provides  that all employees  pay the full
employee  share toward  their  retirement  benefit.  That  contribution  percentage  differs  based on whether
they  are "Classic"  unit  members  or subject  to the Public  Employees'  Pension  Reform  Act  of 2013
("PEPRA")  unit  members.  During  the most  recent  contract  negotiations  between  the  City  and the
Executives  agreed  that  they  would  participate  in  a cost  sharing  program.  The  South  Gate  Police
Management  Association  ("SGPMA")  was  the  first  labor  group  to participate  in the  cost  sharing
program  by having  all their "Classic"  unit  members  contribute  2% of their  salary  toward  the City's
share  of  their  retirement  benefits  beginning  in  FY  2022-23.  The  final  ordinance  amending  the

  l

  9
 CalPERS  contract  for the cost sharing  program  with  SGPMA  was approved  by the City  Council  at its
February  14, 2023 meeting.

The  other  employee  associations,  the  Miscellaneous  Employees'  Association  ("MEA"),  the
Professional  Mid-Management  Association  ("PMMA"),  the  Division  Managers'  Association
("DMA"),  and  the  Police  Officers'  Association  ("POA"),  followed  with  members  agreeing  to
participate  in the cost sharing  program  by contributing  1% of their  salary  toward  the City's  share of
their  retirement  benefits  beginning  in  FY  2023-24.  The  final  ordinance  amending  the  CalPERS
contract  for the cost sharing  program  with  MEA,  PMMA,  DMA,  and POA  was approved  by the City
Council  at its June 13, 2023  meeting.  The  cost  sharing  program  for  each  of these  labor  groups  is
pursuant  to California  Government  Code 20516(a)  and was effective  in July 2023.

Staff began  working  with  CalPERS  to amend  the City's  contract  to implement  this change  in August
2023 and received  approval  and the necessary  information  to move  forward  on September  6, 2023.

The cost sharing  arrangement  has already  been approved  by the City  Council  on September  13, 2022,
by  resolution  approving  the  updated  salary  tables  and  benefits  for  unrepresented  executive
management  contract  employees,  Resolution  No. 2022-54-CC.  In order to proceed  with  amending  the
City's  contract  with  CalPERS  for cost sharing,  CalPERS  requires  a Resolution  of Intention,  an election
of employees  agreeing  to the  contract  change,  and adoption  of an ordinance  amending  the  City's
contract  with  CalPERS.  This  amendment  would  ultimately  bring  the CalPERS  contract  in alignment
with  Resolution  No. 2022-54-CC.

The  CalPERS  contract  amendment  is straightforward;  the  only  change  is that  it will  provide  for
employee  cost sharing  of 1% for unclassified  executive  and top-level  management  contract  employees.
The additional  amounts  paid by the employee  toward  the City's  contribution  will  be credited  to each
member's  PERS  account  as normal  contributions  and  will  allow  the  City  to  process  the  full
contribution  as tax deferred  compensation  in accordance  with  IRC414(h)(2).

According  to CalPERS  procedures,  an amendment  to the contract  that changes  the employees'  rate of
contribution  requires  a secret ballot  election  among  the employees  affected.  That  election  must  follow
Council  adoption  of  the  Resolution  of  Intention  and  precede  adoption  of  the  final  documents.
Following  the adoption  of this Resolution,  the notice  of election  will  be posted  conspicuously  in the
department  over  a period  of seven  days  that  include  a weekend.  The  CalPERS  contract  cannot  be
amended  if  a majority  of the  affected  members  vote  to disapprove  of  the proposed  plan.  Should
members  of the unrepresented  executive  management  contract  employees  vote  to approve  the cost
sharing  plan  as already  approved  in Resolution  No.  2022-54-CC,  then  staff  will  proceed  with  the
following:

  1.  Introduction  and First Reading  of Ordinance  amending  the CalPERS  contract  at the October  24,
  2023 City  Council  meeting.
  2.  Final  adoption  of Ordinance  at the November  14, 2023 City  Council  meeting.
  3.  Contract  Amendment  effective  December  17, 2023.

Attached  as Exhibit  "A"  is the proposed  CalPERS  Amendment  to Contract  between  the Board  of
Administration  of the California  Public  Employees'  Retirement  System  and the City  Council  of the
City  of South  Gate.  Attached  as Exhibit  "B"  is the Proof  of Publication  for the notice  of this public
hearing.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION  DECLARING  A  CONTINUED  EMERGENCY  AND
AUTHORIZING  REPAIR,  REPLACEMENT  OR  MAINTENANCE  ACTIVITIES  OF
PUBLIC  FACILITIES  RELATED  TO  THE  URBAN  ORCHARD,  CITY  PROJECT  NO.
539-Pa  WITHOUT  PUBLIC  BIDDING,  PURSUANT  TO  THE  EMERGENCY
CONTRACTING  PROCEDURES  OF  THE  SOUTH  GATE  MUNICIPAL  CODE  AND
THE  CALIFORNIA  PUBLIC  CONTRACT  CODE

PURPOSE:  To declare  an emergency  still  exists  and to authorize  the repair,  replacement  or
maintenance  activities  of public  facilities  related  to the Urban  Orchard  Project  without  public
bidding.  The  Los  Angeles  County  Department  of  Public  Health,  Solid  Waste  Division
("County")  issued  a Corrective  Action  Order  requiring  construction  to stop on the project.  The
declaration  of  emergency  is necessary  to  streamline  the  process  to  procure  a replacement
contractor  to provide  maintenance  activities  to preserve  the site in a safe condition  until  the
County  authorizes  construction  work  on the project  to resume.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider  making  a finding  and adopting
a Resolution  declaring  an  emergency  still  exists  and  authorizing  repair,  replacement  or
maintenance  activities  of public  facilities  related  to the Urban  Orchard,  City  Project  No.  539-
PRK,  without  public  bidding,  pursuant  to the emergency  contracting  procedures  of the  South
Gate Municipal  Code and the California  Public  Contract  Code.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no  impact  to  the  General  Fund.  The  Urban  Orchard  Project
("Project")  has received  a total  of $30.5 million  in grant and other funds  for design,  construction,
operations,  and  maintenance,  as summarized  below,  inclusive  of  a $5,000,000  grant  from
Caltrans.

ANALYSIS:  The Project  was under  construction  and approximately  80% of construction  work
has been  completed.  On  December  29,  2022,  the  City  received  a Corrective  Action  Order
("Order")  from  the County.  The Order  required  the City  to stop all construction  activities  until
such a time  as a Post Closure  Land Use Plan ("PCLUP")  for the Project  site was approved  by the
County.  Given  the PCLUP  approval  process  and input  received  to date,  it will  take  at least
several  months,  possibly  six or more,  to obtain  approval.

  1  22
 To  avoid  the  significant  delay  damages  that  would  be payable  by  the  City  to the  general
contractor  during  a prolonged  suspension  of the project  pending  approval  of the PCLUP,  the City
Council  terminated  the  general  contractor's  agreement  at a Special  City  Council  meeting  on
February  6, 2023.  Such termination  provided  both  immediate  and long-term  cost savings  to the
City  but also created  an immediate  need for the City  to retain  an interim  contractor  to perform
certain  ongoing  maintenance  and safety  activities;  a need which  must  be met  sooner  than  the
time necessary  to engage in normal  public  bidding  procedures.

The proposed  Resolution  declares  a continued  emergency  exists pursuant  to the authority  granted
by South Gate Municipal Code 831.54.470 and California Public Contract Code 5322050. Those
Code  Sections  allow  cities,  by resolution,  to approve  the  City's  entry  into  contracts  without
engaging  in public  bidding  where  certain  emergency  conditions  are found  to have occurred.  Staff
continues  to believe  that the County's  Order  directing  all construction  work  to be ceased on the
Project,  constitutes  such an emergency  due to the public's  safety  with  an unfinished  construction
site and the need to respond  accordingly  to additional  directives  given  by the County  related  to
ensuring  public  safety.  Staff  is  recornrnending  that  the  City  Council  adopt  the  proposed
Resolution  so that the City  can avail  itself  of the accelerated  contracting  procedures  authorized
by those  Code  Sections.  The  Resolution,  (1)  declares  an emergency,  (2)  authorizes  the City
Manager  to take  such  actions  deemed  necessary  to  cause  the  maintenance  activities  to  be
performed  and to procure  the necessary  equipment,  services,  and supplies  all  without  giving
notice  for bids for contracts,  (3) requires  that at each regularly  scheduled  City  Council  Meeting,
the  City  Manager  present  to the  Council  the reasons  justifying  why  the emergency  will  not
permit  a delay  resulting  from  a competitive  solicitation  for bids,  why  that action  is necessary  to
respond  to the emergency,  and that the City  Council  review  the emergency  action  to determine,
by a four-fifth's  vote, that there is a need to continue  the emergency  action  until  the emergency
action  is terminated.

The  City  is working  diligently  to secure  the PCLUP  approval.  The process  has been  initiated
with  the  submittal  of technical  documents  such  as the Workplan  for  interim  measures  and a
Summary  of Site Investigation,  and the City  continues  to address  the requirements  imposed  by
the County.

Since  the original  Resolution  declaring  an emergency  was  approved  by the  City  Council  on
February  6, 2023, the following  contracts,  expenditures,  and milestones  have been undertaken:

  1.  NR Development  Inc.,  was informed  that Contract  No. 2021-66-CC  was terminated  by
  the City  Council  effective  February  13, 2023,  except  for maintenance  activities.  Staff
  met with  NR Development  Inc., to discuss  the steps to close out construction  activities
  and continue  maintenance  activities.  As of February  16, 2023, NR Development  Inc., is
  no longer  providing  any project  services  or maintenance  activities.

  2.  City  forces  are providing  maintenance  services  of the site. The site has been secured
  with  perimeter  fencing  and security  contract  services.

  3.  Coordination  with  the  Trust  for  Public  Land  ("TPL")  to  complete  the  process  to
  prepare  the technical  documents  necessary  to secure  a replacement  contractor  was

  2  23
   completed,  Preliminarily  selected  a recommended  interim  contractor;  conducted  a field
  review;  and  received  a fee proposal  for  the  interim  maintenance  and  construction
  activities  approved  by the Local  Enforcement  Agency  ("LEA").  Received  a proposal
  from the contractor  and have begun negotiations.

  4,  Submitted  to the LEA  the Summary  of Investigations  Report,  Workplan  of Interim
  Control  Measures  ("WICM"),  Supplemental  WICM  and Phase II Workplan.  Received
  approval  of the WICM  and conditional  approval  of the Phase II Workplan.  Submitted  a
  revised  WICM  as requested  by the LEA.  Submitted  the revised  Phase II Workplan  on
  April  18, 2023.  On May  9, 2023,  the LEA  approved  the Revised  WICM  for which  the
  safety  measures  were  implemented  by  May  12,  2023.  To  date  three  months  of
  monitoring  have been completed  per the Phase II Workplan.

  5.  Approved  a funding  increase  for TPL  in the amount  of $50,000.  On January  24, 2023,
  the City  Council  approved  a $250,000  budget  for Amendment  No.  6 to Contract  No.
  3352 with  TPL,  however,  Amendment  No. 6 had a budget  requirement  of $300,000.  A
  budget  increase  of $50,000  was administratively  approved  to align  the amount  of the
  budget  authority  with  the $300,000  budget  requirement  for Amendment  No.  6, which
  provides  funding  for the technical  services  required  to comply  with  requirements  from
  the LEA.

  6.  A bid was received  from  LA  Engineering  to complete  the construction  of maintenance
  activities  in  the  WICM  approved  by  the  LEA  for  the  Urban  Orchard  Project.  A
  construction  contract  in the amount  of $2,919,248  was executed  administratively  under
  the authority  granted  by the subject  resolution.

  7.  Construction  work  has  begun.  Progress  to  date  includes  completing  backfill  of
  overflow  structure  at the south  wetland,  and substarxtially  completing  backfill  of the
  reservoir  and  stockpile  management.  Construction  work  has begun  adjacent  to the
  Bandini  Channel.

  8.  Methane  gas monitoring  has begun  and four months  of sampling  have been completed.
  The completed  sampling  results  are scheduled  to be submitted  to the LEA  in January
  2024. There  are 16 probes  throughout  the 7-acre  site. One probe  has detected  traces  of
  methane,  however,  at amounts  below  regulatory  requirements.

BACKGROUND:  The Project  is a part of the FY 2022/23  Capital  Improvement  Program.  The
Project  is located  between  the Los  Angeles  River,  Firestone  Boulevard,  the Thunderbird  Villa
Mobile  Home  Park,  and the I-710  Freeway.  Two  primary  purposes  of the Project  are to divert
and treat storm water  run-off  from  the Los Angeles  River  and provide  recreation  opportunities  to
South Gate residents.

The Project  is being  constructed  on a property  that was used as an unpermitted  landfill  until  1949
by an entity  known  as Southeastern  Disposal  and By-Products.  The property  site is identified  in
CalRecycle's  Solid  Waste  Information  System  ("SWIS")  as an Unpertnitted  Closed  Solid  Waste
Disposal  Site and SWIS  No. 19-AA-5545.  In 1984,  the State of California  Department  of Health

  3  24
 Services,  Toxic  Substances  Control  Division  concluded  that  the  clean-up  work  completed
effectively  mitigated  waste  constituents  to  proceed  with  the  Lewis  Homes  residential
development  project.  The requirements  of the PCLUP  came into  effect  in 1988. As such, the
project site is subject to State solid waste regulations that require the PCLUP  before any change
to the current land use, construction,  or land preparation can occur.

The Los Angeles  County  Department  of Public  Health,  Solid Waste Management  Program,  acts
as the LEA  for the State of California's  Department  of Resources  Recycling  and Recovery
("CalRecycle").  The  County  is authorized  by  Division  30 of  the  Public  Resources  Code
("PRC"),  Section  43209  and 45000,  Title  14 and 27 of the California  Code of Regulations  (14
CCR & 27 CCR),  to enforce  applicable  solid waste regulations  and to ensure solid waste sites
meet the state minimum  standards within the County  of Los Angeles.  As such, the City  is
working with the LEA to obtain approval of the PCLUP.

Construction  is  currently  at  the  80%  completion  stage.  Improvements  that  have  been
substantially  completed  include,  but are not limited  to, rough grading,  drop inlet for storm water
diversion  structures  in the Bandini  Channel,  a wetland  overlook  area, the stream adjacent  to the
educatioi'i/flexible  space building  and wetland,  south  bio  swale,  construction  of  18  raised
planters,  planting  of  75  trees,  installation  of  the  prefabricated  education  center  and  the
restroom/maintenance  building,  two  shade  structures,  a water  element  at the  playground,
installation  of multi-use  walking  and bicycle  pathways,  exercise  equipment  located  at various
stages along the walking  and bicycle  paths, benches, picnic  tables, drinking  fountains,  trash cans,
and pathway  lighting. The total estimated  cost of improvements  completed  to date is over $12
million.

The Project has received  the listed grants. The process has begun to enter into an agreement  with
Caltrans to receive an additional  $5 million  for a grand total of $30.5 million.

  EXISTS  AND  AUTHORIZING  REPAIR,  RF,PLACEMENT  OR
  MAINTENANCE  ACTIVITIES  OF PUBLIC  FACILITIES  RELATED  TO
  THE  URBAN  ORCHARD  PROJECT  WITHOUT  PUBLIC  BIDDING,
  PURSUANT  TO THE  EMERGENCY  CONTRACTING  PROCEDURES  OF
  THE  SOUTH  GATE  MUNICIPAL  CODE  AND  THE  CALIFORNIA
  PUBLIC  CONTRACT  CODE

  WHEREAS,  at the Special  City Council  meeting  on February  6, 2023, the City Council
for the City of South Gate ("City")  considered  and passed a Resolution  declaring  an emergency
and authorized  the repair, replacement  or maintenance  activities  of public  facilities  related to the
Urban Orchard  Project ("Project") pursuant to the emergency contracting  procedures  of the South
Gate Municipal  Code and the California Public Contract Code;

  WHERF,AS,  construction  activities  at the Project  site began on August  2, 2021, and have
reached the eighty percent  completion  stage, but the Project  will  require  several more months  of
work before it is complete;

  WHEREAS,  the City has received  notice  from  the Los Angeles  County  Department  of
Public  Health,  Solid  Waste  Management  Program  ("County"),  demanding  that  the  City
immediately  cease all construction  work  on the Project  until  such time that a Post Closure  Land
Use Plan ("PCLUP")  is submitted  to the County  for approval  before any change to the current land
use, construction,  or land preparation  can occur to comply  with the requirements  of the California
Code of Regulations,  Title  27 (27 CCR),  Section  21190  (the "Cease  and Desist  and Corrective
Action Order");

  WHEREAS,  the City has terminated its construction agreement withthe  contractor,  except
for the requirement  for the contractor to perform certain maintenance activities;

  WHEREAS,  although  no construction  activities  will  occur  at the Project  site until  the
County  issues its PCLUP,  it will  be necessary  in the interim  for certain  minimal  maintenance
activities to be performed  at the site for the protection of the existing  improvements  and/or  for
public safety (collectively,  the "Maintenance  Activities");

  WHEREAS,  at a special  meeting  of the South Gate City  Council  ("Council")  held on
Monday,  February  6, 2023, the Council  received  information  provided  by the City's  Public  Works
Department  establishing  that  the  City  does  not  have  sufficient  manpower  to perform  the
Maintenance  Activities  with  its own forces,  and that the immediate  need for the performance  of
the Maintenance  Activities  does not  permit  a delay  that  would  result  from  a competitive
solicitation for bids; and

has been initiated  with  the submittal  of technical  documents  such as the Workplan  for  interim
measures  and a Surnrnary  of Site Investigation,  and the City  continues  to address the requirements
imposed  by the County.

NOW,  THEREFOR,  BASED  ON THF,  FACTS  SET FORTH  ABOVE,  THE  COUNCIL  OF
THE  CITY  OF  SOUTH  GATE,  CALIFORNIA,  HEREBY  MAKES  THE  FOLLOWING
FINDINGS:

  1.  The County's  issuance  of the Cease and Desist  and Corrective  Action  Order  at the
  current  stage of the Project  work,  coupled  with  the immediate  and ongoing  need to
  perform  the Maintenance  Activities,  has created  an emergency  for the City  with

  bids to perform  the Maintenance  Activities;  and

  3.  The actions  to be taken pursuant  to the Resolutions  set forth  below  continue  to be
  necessary  to respond  to the emergency;  and

  4.  The City is working  diligently  to secure the PCLUP  approval.  The process  has been
  initiated  withthe  submittal  oftechnical  documents  such as the Workplan  for interim
  measures  and a Summary  of Site Investigation,  and the City  continues  to address
  the requirements  imposed  by the County.

  SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION  AUTHORIZING  THE  TERMINATION  OF  THE  ECO-
  RAPID  TRANSIT,  FORMERI-Y  KNOWN  AS  THE  ORANGELINE  DEVELOPMENT
  AUTHORITY,  JOINT  POWERS  AUTHORITY

  PURPOSE:  To formally  recognize  the tertnination  of the Eco-Rapid  Transit,  which  is a Joint
  Powers  Authority  ('JPA")  established  in 2005  by several  cities  interested  cities  in the advocacy
  relating  to the development  of the West Santa Ana Branch  Transit  Corridor.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Adopting  a Resolution  authorizing  the City's  appointee  to the Eco-Rapid  Transit  ("ERT")
  to  vote  to  terminate  the  JPA  under  Section  3.2(i)  of  the  Joint  Powers  Authority
  Agreement;  and
  b.  Authorizing  the  City  Manager  to  take  steps  to  complete  the  City  of  South  Gate
  withdrawal  from  the ERT.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  The withdrawal  from  the ERT  will  have no fiscal  impact  beyond  the dues
  the City  has paid  for  Fiscal  Year  2023-24.  While  the City  has paid  an annual  fee to ERT  of
  approximately  $34,000,  it is anticipated  that  the  Gateway  Cities  Council  of  Governments
  ("COG")  may  establish  a fee  for  participation  by  those  cities  on its newly  created  WSAB
  Corridor  Committee  which  will  be taking  over the advocacy  efforts  from  the ERT.  At this time,
  there  has been  no  indication  of  the  amount  of  any  annual  fee  that  the  COG  may  assess.
  Currently,  the ERT  dues are paid  through  special  transit  revenue  sources  and not the General
  Fund.

  ANALYSIS:  The ERT,  which  was originally  known  as the Orangeline  Development  Authority,
  was established  in 2005  to advocate  with  entities  and agencies  such as the Los Angeles  County
  Metropolitan  Transportation  Authority  ("Metro"),  for the development  of the West  Santa  Ana
  Branch  Transit  Corridor  ("WSAB")  and other issues that may benefit  the communities  along that
  corridor  relating  to the proposed  light  rail line.

  The ERT  has been a critical  voice  in the advocacy  with  Metro  on prioritizing  the WSAB  light
  rail,  The goal of providing  a light  rail  system  to the southeast  region  has been a priority  for the

  1

  29
 12 member  communities  for nearly  two  decades.  Without  continued  advocacy,  it is likely  the
WSAB  project  may fall further  behind  and may not remain  one of the highest  priorities  for Metro
in its recent  strategic  plan.  Metro  is currently  in the environmental  clearance  evaluation  process
under  the California  Environmental  Quality  Act  (CEQA)  and the National  Environment  Policy
Act  (NEPA).  Those  processes  should  be completed  in late 2024.  Upon  completion,  Metro  can
proceed  with  a number  of steps,  such as obtaining  bids  for the project  and acquiring  assets to
make the corridor  possible.

While  the East  Santa  Ana  Branch  ("ESAB")  is projected  to start  in the City  of Artesia  and
tei'minate  at Union  Station  in Los Aiigeles,  it is being  designed  and constructed  in two  phases.
The first  phase will  run from  Artesia  to Slauson  where  the A Line  is (formerly  the Blue  Line).
This 14.5-mile  segment  is estimated  to cost approximately  $9 billion.

The advocacy  for the WSAB  will  not end with  the termination  of ERT  but will  be merged  into
the COG.  Given  that the current  stage of the WSAB  project  is in planning,  and the suppoit  of
Metro  to prioritize  this  project,  advocacy  by the  COG  will  change  to representing  impacted
communities  on more  technical  elements  of the project.  Such  elements  will  include  achial
infrastructure  elements  within  the  communities,  3%  local  match  requirements,  and  station
designs;  to mention  a few.

The City  has been paying  aru'iual dues since the inception  of ERT  in 2005.  Those  dues in recent
years have been approximately  $34,000,  annually.  With  the transition  to the COG,  the plan is to
establish  a committee  made  up of the impacted  communities  to provide  guidance  to the COG
leadership  on matters  relating  to the WSAB  project.  Annual  dues assessed upon  the City  will
support  the new duties  associated  with  the COG  efforts.

BACKGROUND:  The  ERT  Joint  Powers  Authority  was originally  established  in 2005.  The
ERT  is fortned  under  Government  Code  Section  6500.  Under  the adopted  bylaws  of the ERT,
Section  3.2(i)  provides  for  the  Authority  to be terminated  upon  the unanimous  vote  of  its
members  or at such time there is only  one member  remaining.  Under  state law, any debts are the
sole responsibility  of the JPA  and are not the responsibility  of the member  agencies.  At this
time,  it is not anticipated  there will  be any outstanding  debts or assets when the ERT  dissolves.

The COG  is expected  to establish  the new WSAB  Committee  in early 2024.

  PURPOSE:  Tocreatethefull-timepositionsofCourtLiaisonOfficerandRecordsManagement
  Technician  - Police  in the Police  Department;  approve  the job specifications  for the full-time  Court
  Liaison  Officer  and Records  Management  Technician  - Police  positions;  and add the full-time
  court  Liaison  Officer  and  Records  Management  Technician  - Police  classifications  to  the
  consolidated  salary pay table with  the proposed  salary range.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider  adopting  a Resolution  amending
  Resolution  No. 6454 (Salary  Resolution  and Position  Classification  Plan) by taking  the following
  actions:
  1)  Create the full-time  position  of Court  Liaison  Officer  in the Police  Department;
  2)  Approve  the classification  specification  for the full-time  position  of Court  Liaison  Officer;
  3)  Update  the Consolidated  Salary  Pay Table  for the City  of South  Gate by adding  the full-
  time position  of Court  Liaison  Officer  at Pay Grade 516 ($4,440  - $5,397  monthly),  a Non-
  Exempt  Classification  assigned  to the Municipal  Employees  Association  ("MEA");
  4)  Create  the full-time  position  of Records  Management  Technician  - Police  in the Police
  Department;
  5)  Approve  the classification  specification  for the full-time  position  of Records  Management
  Technician  - Police;  and
  6)  Update  the Consolidated  Salary  Pay Table  for the City  of South  Gate by adding  the full-

  1

  62
   time position of Records Management Technician - Police at Pay Grade 541 ($5,332
  $6,482 monthly), a Non-Exempt Classification assigned to MEA.

FISCAL IMPACT:  The cost to add the full-time Court Liaison Officer position is estimated to
be $80,865 annually, which includes the cost of benefits, and the cost to add the full-time Records
Management Technician - Police is estimated to be $97,230 annually, which includes the cost of
the benefits. The addition of the full-time  Court Liaison Officer and Records Management
Technician - Police positions will not result in any additional costs since both positions  were
approved as part of the Adopted FY 2023/24 Fiscal Year.

ANALYSIS:  None,

 BACKGROUND:  The City must, from time to time, add, remove, reclassify, or otherwise adjust
job classifications, job specifications and/or compensation in the Salary Resolution and Position
 Classification Plan in order to satisfy the changing needs and demands of the City's workforce.  In
response to these changing needs and demands, job classification specifications must be amended
to more closely match the tasks which need to be performed by employees in the City's various
departments.

The Court Liaison Officer, identified in the FY 2023/24 Adopted Budget as "Court Officer," will
primarily serve as the point of contact between the courts and the Police Department, while
performing a variety of responsible, sensitive, confidential, non-sworn specialized duties related
to the filing of criminal cases. The position will be responsible for quality control of reports
generated by police personnel and will coordinate the paperwork forwarded to the District
Attorney's Officer for review of criminal complaints and prosecutions. The position will also assist
with responsible administrative  and support duties, as well as independently  organizing  and
completing  assigned  tasks.

The proposed pay is based upon the hourly wages of the part-time Court Liaison Officer translated
to the full-time salary equivalent, which supports this recommendation.  Accordingly,  it is
recommended that the full-time  Court Liaison Officer position be paid at Pay Grade 516 ($4,440
- $5,397 per month).

The Records Management position will perform moderately complex and confidential duties and
is generally responsible for public records requests and other types of digital evidence collected
by the Police Department. The position will assist with certain administrative and supportive duties
in the conduct of City business and will independently organize and complete assigned tasks. The
position will also be responsible for handling confidential  matters.

The proposed pay is based on similar Technician classifications within the City to support this
recommendation.  Accordingly,  it is recommended that the full-time  Records Management
Technician - Police be paid at Pay Grade 541 ($5,332 - $6,482 per month).

Human Resources staff worked with the Police Department to develop the job classification
specifications for the Court Liaison Officer and Records Management Technician - Police. Staff

  2

  63
 also worked  with MEA  to review  the new job specifications  and the recommended  pay, of which
they agree.

 SUBJECT:  OPTION AGREEMENT  WITH PRIMESTOR  DEVELOPMENT,  LLC., TO
 PURCHASE  A CITY OWNED PROPERTY  LOCATED  AT 4909 MASON  STREET,
 SOUTH GATE, CALIFORNIA, ASSESSOR PARCEL N0. 6216-032-900

 P{JRPOSE: To consider approving an Option Agreement with Primestor Development,  LLC,,
 for the purchase of City owned property located at 4909 Mason Street, South Gate, California.

 RECOMIV[ENDED  ACTION: The City Council will consider approving an Option Agreement
 with Primestor Development, LLC., to purchase City owned property at 4909 Mason Street,
 Assessor  Parcel No. 6216-032-900.

 FISCAL IMPACT:  Primestor Development, LLC., ("Optionee or Primestor") will pay a non-
 refundable fee of $25,000 to the City ("Optionor") upon approval by the City Council of the
 Option Agreement. Should the Optionee exercise the Option, then it will pay the fair market
 price established by an independent MAI appraisal at the time the Option is exercised.

 ANALYSIS:  Primestor is a successful development company of both commercial and housing
 in Los Angeles County. The City and Primestor have partnered before with the development  of
 the azalea Shopping  Center.

 The property in question is owned by the City and is currently used to store material like sand
 and dirt used by the City's Public Works Department. The property is nearly landlocked  with
 the only access being provided by a narrow alley known as Neville Avenue. To the northeast of
 the property lies the UPR and fuhire West Santa Ana Branch ("WASB") Light Rail right-of-way,
 To the southwest of the property is a commercial property containing Riccos Ice; to the east is an
 auto repair shop (Diamond Touch Body Shop); and to the west is another auto repair facility
 (Muse Autoproject).  This property owned by the City is in the future Gateway Specific Plan
 ("Specific Plan") area which will be developed to take advantage of the future light rail station
 that will  be built  at the location.

 Currently, the area is dominated by light industrial uses along with auto repair uses. The future
 Specific Plan will likely change that dynamic with commercial and housing. The City is getting

  81
 ready to undertake  a Metro  TOD-SIP  planning  which  will  be the beginning  steps for the Specific

Plan.  It is anticipated  the development  of the Specific  Plan will  take up to 24 months  to finish.

The Optionee  is required  to develop  the property  consistent  with  the future  Specific  Plan, should

it exercise  the Option  Agreement.  In addition,  the Optionee  is required  to cooperate  with  the

City  in the development  of the Specific  Plan, should  it be asked.

Metro  hopes the WSAB  project  environmental  clearances  will  be finalized  by late 2024.  Should

Metro  obtain  those  clearances,  then  it will  begin  any  property  acquisition  it may  need  to

undertake  the project.  That property  acquisition  may include  portions  of the City  property  which

abut the rail right-of-way.  The Optionee  is aware of that possibility,  and it is included  within  the
Option Agreement.

Should  the agreement  be approved,  Primestor  will  begin  trying  to assemble  other properties  and

undertaking  certain  environmental  shidies  such  as Phases  I and  II  analyses.  The  Option

Agreement  provides  the Optionee  with  up to 25 months  to exercise  the option  to purchase  with

the ability  to extend  for  a total  of 18 months.  This  is necessary  given  the uncertainty  of the

specificity  of  when  the  Specific  Plan  will  be  approved,  and  when  Metro  will  begin  the

constniction  of the WSAB  project.  The base term within  the Option  Agreement  and the potential
extensions  should  provide  a sufficient  amount of time for both activities  to occur.

The  City  did  list  the properiy  with  the  Califomia  Department  of Housing  and Community

Development  in  accordance  with  the  Surplus  Land  Act  ("SLA").  Primestor  was  the  only

submitter  and the City  Council  authorized  staff  to begin  negotiations.  Those  negotiations  are

reflected  within  the  proposed  Option  Agreement.  The  Optionee  understands  the  adopted

inclusionary  housing  requirement  and any housing  elements  within  the future  Specific  Plan will

also reflect  those standards.  All SLA  related  compliance  documents  are maintained  by the
Community  Development  Department.

 PURPOSE:  To purchase four  electric  Ford F-150  pickups  for the Water  Division  of the
 Department  of Public Works.

 RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council will consider:
  a.  ApprovingthePurchaseOrderagreementwithNormReevesFordforFour(4)FordF-150
  Pickup Trucks, in an amount not-to-exceed $262,915, for the Water Division  of the
  Department  of Public  Works;

  b.  Appropriating$2,915inWaterFundstofullyfundthe$262,915purchaseprice;and
  c.  Authorizing the City Manager to execute the documents necessary to purchase the vehicles
  in forms acceptable  to the City Attorney.

 FISCAL  IMPACT:  There is no impact to the General Fund. The cost of the four trucks is
 $262,915 and will be funded with Water Funds, of which $260,000 is budgeted in the Fiscal Year
 2023/24 0perating Budget. An appropriation is required in the amount of $2,915 to fully fund the
 purchase.

 ANALYSIS:  The Water Division utilizes F150 pickup trucks for its distribution and production
 operations.  Four are in need of replacement due to age based on the recommendations from the
 Fleet  Master  Plan.

 Staff recommends purchasing four electric Ford F-150 pickups to replace the current aging units.
 Each pickup truck's price is $65,729, which includes equipment that is needed for operations such
 as safety lighting and toolboxes for storage, as noted on the quote in Attachment A. After Council
 approval, the trucks will be ordered and delivered by the Summer of 2024.

 The City's purchasing policy requires three bids to procure vehicles. Staff reached out to three
 dealerships for quotes and only received one quote per vehicle due to supply chain issues occurring
 with auto dealers. Staff recommends that the vehicles be purchased without further bidding under
 the exemptions provided by Section 1.54.510 of the South Gate Municipal Code, which provides
 exemptions from formal and informal bidding procedures. The code stipulates an exemption is
 allowed from bidding when competition for formal bids does not exist, further, when the director

  91
 of finance  determines,  with  the concurrence  of the city  manager,  that due to the nature  of the
supplies,  equipment  or services,  formal  bidding  is not likely  to result  in the lowest  price.  The City
Manager  and Director  of Administrative  Services  concur  an exemption  is warranted  due to the
supply  chain  issues  occurring  and the inability  of auto dealers  to provide  quotes  which  do not
produce  a competitive  price  opportunity.

BACKGROUND:  The Department  of Public  Works  operates  a fleet  of 90 vehicles  which  are
utilized  for the operations  and maintenance  of City  infrastructure.  Reliability  of the fleet is key to
ensuring  infrastructure  is properly  maintained  and managed.

The Department  prepared  a Fleet  Master  Plan  ("Plan").  The Plan  aims  to reduce  the costs  of
operating  and maintaining  the City's  fleet of vehicles  and to provide  safe, reliable,  and productive
vehicles.  The Plan provides  recommended  life cycles for vehicle  replacements.  Replacing  vehicles
according  to recornrnended  life cycles  allows  for the lowest  cost of ownership.  New  vehicles  offer
benefits  such as reliability,  reduced  :tuel consumption  and emissions,  and increased  safety  due to
more airbags,  safety  sensors,  and rear-view  cameras.

The proposed  vehicle  replacement  is consistent  with  the Plan. The proposed  trucks  will  support
the Water  Division  and will  be used for jobs  such as valve  replacements,  emergency  water  main
breaks,  and meter  readings.  The proposed  vehicle  replacement  plan is listed  below.

 ANALYSIS:  The Public  Contract  Code  sets requirements  that the City  must  abide  by prior  to
making  final  payment  on constructionprojects.  Public  Contract  Code Section  7107 establishes  that
the City  must  accept  the completion  of construction  and issue public  notice  of such prior  to
releasing  final  payment  (known  as the retention  payment).  This process  is a mechanism  to provide
written  notice  (Notice  of Completion)  to concerned  parties  that all work  on the project  has been
completed.  The Notice  of Completion  initiates  the period  within  which  concerned  parties  may
exercise  their  lien rights  for the work  they performed  on the project.  The City  may use a part,  or
all, of the retention  payment  to settle any liens exercised  against  the City.

BACKGROUND:  The  South  Gate  Police  Department  Detective  Bureau  Remodel  Project
("Project")  is in  the  FY  2022/23  Capital  Improvement  Program  ("CIP").  The  Project  was
implemented  to remodel  the Detective  Bureau.  The improvements  included  new office  furniture,
painting,  replacement  of the carpet  and tile,  construction  of walls  for private  offices,  replacement
of light  fixtures  to energy  saving  LED  fixtures.

On  January  24,2023,  the  City  Council  awarded  Contract  No.  2023-66-CC  to ENL  Building
Services,  Inc.,  in the amount  of $185,045.  Two  contract  change  orders  were  issued.  The  final
contract  amount,  including  the change  orders,  is $184,366.

In addition  to the subject  contract,  additional  expenditures  were incurred  for design,  to purchase
office  'furniture,  for  network  improvements,  inspection  services  and project  management/staff
time.  The final  construction  cost was $452,009.

Construction  of the  Project  began  June  5, 2023,  and  was  completed  on July  14,  2023.  The
Contractor  has met all of the contract  obligations  and the work  was performed  in accordance  with
the approved  specifications  with  acceptable  quality  and workmanship,  within  budget,  and on time.

The City  Council  may now  accept  the Project  as completed.  The Notice  of Completion  can now
be filed  with  the Los Angeles  County  Registrar  Recorder's  Office.

SUBJECT:  NOTICE  OF  COMPLETION  FOR  THE  CONSTRUCTION  OF  THE
CITYWIDE  VALVE  REPLACEMENT  PROJECT,  CITY  PROJECT  NO.  688-WTR

PURPOSE:  Construction  of the Citywide  Valve  Replacement  Project  ("Project")  is completed
and the retention  payment  to the contractor  is due.  Section  7107  of the Public  Contract  Code
requires  the City  to accept  completion  of the project  and issue  public  notice  of such, prior  to
releasing  the retention  payment.

RECO!VIMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
a,  Accepting  completion  of construction  of the Citywide  Valve  Replacement  Project  City
  Project  No. 688-WTR,  effective  September  12, 2023;  and
b.  Directing  the City  Clerk  to file a Notice  of Completion  with  Los Angeles  County  Registrar
  Recorder's  Office.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.  The Project  is budgeted  in the
amount  of $465,000  in Water  Funds,  and final  project  costs are summarized  below:

  Project  Expenditures  Budget
  Design  Phase  $10,000
  Construction Contract No. 2022-29-CC  $194,500
  Change Order No. l (Actual Cost)  *$104,389
  Construction  Management  $25,000
  City Staff Inspection Time  $5,000
  Total  $338,889
  * The achial  Change  Order  amount  approved  by the City  Council  was
  $190,000,  however,  work  was completed  under  budget.

ANALYSIS:  The Public  Contract  Code  sets requirements  that the City  must  abide  by prior  to
making  final payment  on construction  projects.  Public  Contract  Code Section  7107 establishes  that
the City  must  accept  the completion  of construction  and issue  public  notice  of such prior  to
releasing  final payment  (known  as the retention  payment).  This process  is a mechanism  to provide
written  notice  (Notice  of Completion)  to concerned  parties  that all work  on the project  has been
completed.  The Notice  of Completion  initiates  the period  within  which  concerned  parties  may
exercise  their  lien rights  for the work  they performed  on the project.  The City  may use a part, or
all, of the retention  payment  to settle any liens exercised  against  the City.

  1  103
 BACKGROUND:  The City  owns and operates  a municipal  water  system  that has approximately
135 miles  of water mains  equipped  with water valves.  This Project  was added to the CIP to replace
deficient  water valves  located  at the intersection  of Southern  Avenue and Kauffman  Avenue. The
Project  included  the installation  of two (2) 24-inch  and one (l)  16-inch  valves,  the replacement  of
an existing  6-inch  fire hydrant  valve,  and three (3) line stops.

On May  10, 2022,  the City  Council  awarded  a contract  to Gentry  General  Engineering,  Inc.,  for
construction  of the Project  in the amount  of $194,500.  A contract  change  order  in the amount  of
$190,000  was approved  by the City  Council  on March  14, 2023,  to install  an additional  24" gate
valve  and one line stop. Though  the revised  contract  amount  was $384,500,  work  was completed
under budget  and the final  construction  cost was $298,889.

Construction  of the Project  began February  2023 and was completed  on September  12, 2023. The
Contractor  has met  all the contract  obligations.  Work  was performed  in accordance  with  the
approved  specifications  with  acceptable  quality  and workmanship  within  budget  and time.

The City  Council  may now  accept the Citywide  Valve  Replacement  Project  as completed  and the
Notice  of Completion  can now be filed  with  the Los Angeles  County  Registrar  Recorder's  Office.

CALL  TO ORDER  Maria del Pilar Avalos,  Mayor  called  a Regular  City  Council  Meeting  to
  order to 6:35 p.m.

PRESENT  Mayor  Maria  del Pilar Avalos,  Vice Mayor  Hurtado,  Council  Member
  Joshua  Barron,  and Council  Member  Maria  Davila;  City Treasurer  Jose De
  La Paz, City  Manager  Chris  Jeffers,  City Attorney  Raul F. Salinas

ABSENT/EXCUSE  Council  Member  Al Rios

1
PERSONNEL  BENEFITS/

RETIREMENT  ADMIN  The City  Council  conducted  a public  hearing  and adopted  Resolution  No.
  2023-69-CC  entitled  Resolution  of the City  Council  of the City  of South
  Gate, California,  giving  notice  of the City's  intention  to approve  an
  amendment  to the contract  between  the City  and the Board  of
  Administration  of the California  Public  Employees'  Retirement  System
  (CalPERS)  to provide  employee  cost sharing  of 1% for the unrepresented
  executive  management  contract  employees  effective  on December  17,
  2023,  by motion  of Council  Member  Davila  and seconded  by Vice  Mayor
  Hurtado.

  Jon Hamilton,  Director  of Human  Resources,  explained  the process  of
  amending  this request  to provide  certain  pension  benefits  to employees
  and once this is approved  the next step would  be the Introduction  and first
  reading  of the ordinance  to proceed  with  the amendment  to our contract
  with  CalPERS.  He stated the departments  that agreed for the cost sharing
  program  that will  provide  those benefits  to employees.

  ROLL  CALL:  Council  Member  Barron,  yes; Council  Member  Davila,
  yes; Vice  Mayor  Hurtado,  yes; Mayor  Avalos,  yes; Council  Member  Rios,
  absent.

COMMENTS  FROM  THE
AUDIENCE  (NON-AGENDA

ITEMS)  Juan Ramon  Cortez,  9637 South Lake Ave,  spoke on tree trimming  and
  his confusion  as to why  only  a certain  part of the street was trimmed.
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF  OCTOBER  10, 2023

COMMENTS  FROM  THE
AUDIENCE  (NON-AGENDA

ITEMS)  CONT'D  Sandra  Hernandez,  10336  Pinehurst  Ave,  spoke  of her concerns  on her

  high-water  bill  of $1,047  when  she normally  paid  between  $50-$150
  monthly.  She mentioned  being  told  she could  not reach  Mayor  Avalos  or

  City  Council  Members  about  the issue  and should  address  her concerns
  with  the water  department.

  Eddie  Hankins,  10431  St. James  Ave,  echoed  similar  concerns  on the

  high-water  bill.

  Ruben  Pichardo,  9210  San Gabriel  Ave,  also echoed  concerns  of their

  water  bill  and expressed  frustration  on what  is happening  with  the bills.

  Mario  Dominguez  spoke  of tree trimming  requests  he made  with  Public
  Works  and how  it could  liave  been  a mistake  with  the way  the trees were
  taken  down.

  Thomas  Buckley  echoed  for the residents  that have  experienced  high
  water  bills  and asked  the council  to investigate  this  matter.

  Bill  Wallace  asks residents  to sign  a petition  for property  taxes  of property

  inheritance

  Mayor  Avalos  stated  that the Council  Members  and herself  are always
  available  and should  not be told  by employees  that they  cannot  reach  out

  to them  regarding  Ms.  Hernandez's  statement.

  Arturo  Cervantez,  Director  of Public  Works,  explained  the increase  in the
  water  bills  and stated  they  have  done  an analysis  and only  11 residents  had

  an inegularity.

  Chris  Jeffers,  City  Manager,  suggested  adding  the water  bill  issue to the
  agenda  to have  more  questions  answered.

  Council  Member  Davila  asked  if there  were  still  ARPA  funds  to be able to
  help  with  utilities.

  Mayor  Avalos  stated  that  residents  are being  heard  and they  will  look  into

  the matter.

  Vice  Mayor  Hurtado  stated  that  because  the water  bill  issue  is not on the
  agenda  and cannot  go back  and forth  with  residents  as it could  violate  the

  Brown  Act.  He also echoed  that  the issue  should  be looked  at and that
  residents  are being  heard.

ITEMS)  CONT'D  Mr.  Jeffers  addressed  the difference  between  a bush  and a tree regarding
  Mr.  Cortez's  statement  and there  are different  stages  in the process  of
  trimming.

  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk,  asked  if Mr.  Cortez's  request  can be looked  at as
  he has attended  for the second  time.

REPORTS  AND  COMMENTS

FROM  CITY  OFFICIALS  Mr.  Cervantez  provided  an update  on the tree trimming  process  and how  it
  is determined  for certain  trees to be taken  down  completely  or saved.

  Steve  Costley,  Interim  Director  of Parks  and Recreation,  announced  the
  Azalea  Art  Walk  happening  on Saturday  and upcoming  Halloween  events
  happening  at South  Gate  Park.

  Meredith  Elguira,  Director  of Community  Development,  recognized  the
  homeowners  that won  the Home  Recognition  Program.

  Ms.  Glaze,  City  Clerk  had nothing  to report.

  Jose De La Paz, City  Treasurer,  had nothing  to report.

  Wendy  O'Kelly,  Deputy  Director  of Administrative  Services,  reiterated
  the LIHWAP  program  that can assist  residents  in their  utility  program.

  Mr.  Hamilton  presented  the jobs  currently  available  to apply.

  Darren  Arakawa,  Chief  of Police,  spoke  on the car show  that happened
  over  the weekend  and the pleasant  experience  they  had. He also
  announced  the Pageant  of the Trees  that  will  be occurring  over  the
  Holiday  season.  He reminded  everyone  about  World  Mental  Health  Day
  and keeping  yourself  safe.

  Mr.  Jeffers  recognized  the ELAC  political  science  class  and how  the
  Council  Members  are of service  to them  to speak  on government  topics.
  He also reminded  the public  about  finding  events  around  the city  on South
  Gate  city  website.  He also spoke  on resources  for Mental  Health  and the
  importance  of taking  some  time  to pause  from  life  amid  many  suffering
  around  the world  at this  moment.

  Raul  F. Salinas,  City  Attorney,  echoed  comments  on Mr.  Jeffers'
  statement.

  Mayor  Avalos  acknowledged  the wars  that  are happening  and how  blessed
  we are that we are safe.

FROM  CITY  OFFICIALS

CONT'D  Council  Member  Davila  echoed  Mayor  Avalos'  statement  on how  blessed

  service  in the water  department  and suggested  training.  Her thoughts  and

  prayers  to people  that liave  lost their  life  in recent  accidents.

  Council  Member  Barron  spoke  on the Henry  Gonzalez  renaming  and how

  open-door  policy.

  emphasized  that we are here to provide  service  to the community  and
  should  be treated  in a respectful  manner  and voiced  his support  in the

  healthcare  strike  currently  happening.  He ended  with  recent  accidents  that

  have  taken  lives  of innocent  people  and some  confusion  of maintenance
  work  of Public  Works.

  Mayor  Avalos  stated  that  customer  service  is a staple  in our city  and

  the State of the City  event.  She expressed  safety  when  driving  as there
  have  been more  accidents  taking  the lives  of innocent  people.
